suggestion: Settle the price-data question as a procurement decision, not a modelling one
why_it_improves_decisions: The requirements trace lists 17 rows this pack cannot close for want of a source; the ones that matter most - ROI, the CLV escrow, market-versus-fair decomposition, the favourites-only control, and promotion itself - all name the same single input: a price whose terms permit storage. Until it exists they are unanswerable at any modelling effort level, and the count is recomputed from requirements_trace.csv on every build rather than asserted here.
what_it_unblocks: ROI, CLV escrow (stage 2), market-vs-fair decomposition, favourites-only control, promotion
evidence_needed: A written data-terms position for one or two price sources, plus a storage decision
risk_if_not_done: Every other improvement is measured against a benchmark we cannot see, so effort keeps going into model complexity that cannot be graded
recommended_path: Do not scrape. Decide whether the project may hold prices at all; if yes, choose the minimum source that satisfies terms; if no, freeze the pricing half of the roadmap and say so on the landing page.

suggestion: Turn the injury-report read into a scheduled 3x-per-week capture before the model grows another feature
why_it_improves_decisions: A single capture cannot support a surprise signal, cannot be replayed, and cannot be audited. The report is the only personnel input the league itself publishes, and it is currently read by hand, once.
what_it_unblocks: Surprise-not-level injury signal; designation reliability scoring; point-in-time replay for backtests

risk_if_not_done: The '6 of 254 rows carry a game designation' class of claim stays unrepeatable, and every depth feature stays built on a snapshot nobody can re-read
recommended_path: Two captures per week is enough to start (Wednesday and Friday); the Friday one must be before the final line move.

suggestion: Grade the totals question against a distributional score, not against a made-up benchmark total
why_it_improves_decisions: Totals are the weakest link right now: two estimators, both with a large walk-forward error, and no market to calibrate against. Ranking them by MAE alone invites tuning to noise; the interval score plus coverage is proper and harder to fool.
what_it_unblocks: A defensible collapse decision (T1 vs T2)
evidence_needed: Nothing; both scores are already computed here
risk_if_not_done: The 'publish twice until one wins' rule turns into a coin flip that someone later calls evidence
recommended_path: Require coverage within 5 points of the nominal 80% before declaring a winner.
